exposure: antepartum risk stratification (low-risk vs. high-risk based on antenatal clinical profiles, sociodemographic, obstetric, and medical factors)
outcome: labour interventions (induction, augmentation, mode of delivery)
cohort: The study included 507 women admitted to the labour ward at Lagos State University Teaching Hospital (LASUTH) from May 2019 to April 2022.
finding: High-risk pregnancies were associated with increased maternal and neonatal complications, including higher rates of labour interventions and adverse neonatal outcomes.
mod_finding: High-risk women had significantly higher rates of induction (14.6% vs. 1.2%), oxytocin augmentation (27% vs. 5.3%), and emergency cesarean delivery (39.3% vs. 23.4%) compared to low-risk women.
